core_obligations: Existence (proof lines 6675-6695): compose n tail contractions and n' bridge contractions; property (2) holds for each factor by the two examples and is inherited by compositions.

Fibre analysis of any competitor c (proof lines 6705-6745): fibres are geometrically connected; each fibre is either one point with residue field kappa(y) or a 1-dimensional proper nodal reduced curve of genus 0 (Lemma lemma-automatic and lemma-closed-subscheme-nodal-curve); outside finitely many y_1,...,y_r the map c is finite and an isomorphism.

Rational tails map to points (proof lines 6747-6785): if a tail C mapped onto a component D of Y, then either D would be a rational tail of Y (contradicting ampleness of omega_Y by Lemma lemma-rational-tail-negative) or, when c(x) is a 1-dimensional fibre through the node, X = X_y  union  C forces g = 0; both absurd.

Uniqueness (proof lines 6787-6840): factoring c through the contraction sequence X -> ... -> X_{n+n'}, induction on n (tails), then for n = 0 the identities Gamma(X, omega_X^^tensor m) = Gamma(X_{n'}, omega_{X_{n'}}^^tensor m) = Gamma(Y, omega_Y^^tensor m) from Lemma lemma-contract-gorenstein-canonical with m = 3 and Lemma lemma-rational-bridge-canonical, plus the Proj comparison of Morphisms, Lemma morphisms-lemma-proper-ample-is-proj, give a canonical isomorphism X_{n'} = Y.
proof_roadmap: Existence by combining the tail and bridge contraction lemmas; note property (2) per factor and for compositions.
Set up uniqueness: fibres of c are geometrically connected; classify each fibre as a point or a genus 0 nodal curve; c is an isomorphism off finitely many points.
Show every rational tail of X is contracted to a point (two cases by the position of c(x) on D).
Induct on the number n of tail contractions; then in the tail-free case compare global sections of powers of omega via the projection formula and conclude X_{n'} = Y as Proj.
difficulty_reason: The lemma characterizes the stable model contraction by three properties (statement lines 6650-6666). The proof (lines 6668-6788) has two genuinely different halves: existence is a composition argument for tail and bridge contractions, and uniqueness runs a fibre-by-fibre analysis of an arbitrary competitor (fibre classification via H^1 = 0 and H^0 = kappa(y), nodality and genus 0 of 1-dimensional fibres), a rational-tail-to-point claim proved by a two-case argument against ampleness of omega_Y, and a closing Proj comparison using the projection formula on omega powers. H3: the uniqueness half alone is a research-grade chain of at least four non-formal steps.
